title: DualTimesField: Rethinking Time Series as Continuous-Time Trends and Events
topic: General Machine Learning->Sequential, Network, and Time Series Modeling
claim: A signal is split into a smooth trend field and a sparse residual event field, then recombined for reconstruction.
layout: 3 stacked bands, top-down; blue and red parallel branches with a dashed residual link
description: A wide architecture diagram in three horizontal bands. The top band shows the input multivariate time series as dotted points, filled for training points and hollow for interpolation points, with X = {x(t1),…,x(tN)}. The middle band has two parallel branches. A blue Continuous Time Field handles low-pass filtering, smoothed signal, Fourier feature encoding with a bandwidth limit, two MLPs, a fusion layer and a smooth trend output Φ_CTF. A red Discrete Geometric Field computes the residual r(t) = x(t) − Φ_CTF(t), which a dashed blue arrow feeds in from the CTF output. It then uses a Gabor atom dictionary, an encoder with gating, sparse selection and an MLP to produce the jagged event output Ψ_DGF. The bottom band, Reconstruction & Loss, shows time-frequency localization, scale annealing, the final sum Φ+Ψ and the multi-objective loss. Blue and red color coding guides the eye.
caption: DualTimesField architecture. The CTF (blue) models smooth trends with bandwidth-limited encoding, while the DGF (red)
abstract: Effective time series representation is critical for revealing temporal dynamics in many fields. However, existing approaches encounter fundamental limitations. Discrete-time representations struggle with irregular sampling and the tradeoff of fidelity and efficiency, while traditional implicit neural representations suffer from spectral bias and frequency entanglement. To address these challenges, we conceptualize time series as the superposition of continuous trends and discrete events from a continuous-time perspective and propose DualTimesField, a framework that utilizes dual implicit neural fields. Its Continuous Time Field captures smooth trends through bandwidth-limited parameterization, while a Discrete Geometric Field models transient events using learnable Gabor atoms, gated sparsity, and coarse-to-fine scale annealing. This explicit field separation effectively overcomes both limitations. Experiments on nine real-world benchmarks demonstrate substantial improvements in representation fidelity, achieving 51.2% average MSE reduction over discrete-time baselines and competitive interpolation on irregular data. Code is available at https://github.com/WisdomTogether/DualTimesField.
